Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for seeing this 33-year-old gentleman for an outpatient neuromuscular evaluation. He reports that his physical concerns first became apparent during childhood, with initial changes noted around 9 years of age. 

He currently works as an accountant, does not smoke, and takes no routine prescription medications. His family history is non-contributory, with no reported neuromuscular disorders among first-degree relatives. Review of systems is negative for any muscle pain, and he experiences no muscle stiffness or cramping. 

On physical examination, cranial nerves II through XII are intact. Motor examination demonstrates normal bulk without any hypertrophy of the calves, and muscle tone is preserved throughout. Manual muscle testing shows 5/5 strength across all major proximal and distal muscle groups. Sensory examination to light touch, temperature, and proprioception is entirely normal. Inspection of both feet reveals prominent high plantar arches. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric, and his gait is normal. 

Recent blood tests are notable for a high serum creatine kinase level, which was measured at 620 U/L and remained elevated on repeat testing. His complete blood count, basic metabolic panel, and thyroid function tests were all unremarkable. 

I would appreciate your expert assessment and recommendations regarding further evaluation for this patient. 

Kind regards,

Dr. Marcus Hayes, MD
Internal Medicine
